title: Knowledge-based_configuration
summary:
Knowledge-based configuration, also referred to as product configuration or product customization, is an activity of customising a product to meet the needs of a particular customer. The product in question may consist of mechanical parts, services, and software.

Configuration systems, also referred to as configurators or mass customization toolkits, are one of the most successfully applied artificial intelligence technologies. Examples include the automotive industry, the telecommunication industry, the computer industry, and power electric transformers.

Starting with rule-based approaches such as R1/XCON, model-based representations of knowledge have been developed that strictly separate product knowledge from reasoning. Core configuration tasks include guiding the user and checking the consistency of user requirements with the knowledge base, solution presentation, and translation of configuration results into bill of materials (BOM). Configuration knowledge bases are composed of a formal description of the structure of the product and further constraints restricting the possible feature and component combinations.

One of the seminal systems was R1 (later known as XCON), developed by John McDermott at Carnegie Mellon University starting in 1978 for Digital Equipment Corporation to automate the configuration of VAX computer systems. This production-rule-based system, implemented in OPS5, demonstrated the feasibility of knowledge-based approaches. Numerous practical configuration problems can be analyzed by the theoretical framework of Najmann and Stein. One important result is that typical optimization problems (e.g., finding a cost-minimal configuration) are NP-complete, making heuristic configuration algorithms the preferred choice for complex artifacts.

Recently, knowledge-based configuration has been extended to service and software configuration. Modeling software configuration has been based on two main approaches: feature modeling and component-connectors. The Kumbang domain ontology combines these approaches building on the tradition of knowledge-based configuration.
